# Simulate one generation
There was an error because some values were negative. That's why we put the max() at some places. 

```{r}
# Simulate WT-Population without any mutations and stochasticity
simulate_one_gen <- function(N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu){
  N_a0 <- max(N_a0, 0)
  New_jtM <- rpois(1, N_a0 * mu * R_a)
  N_jt <- max(rpois(1, R_a * N_a0) - New_jtM, 0) #calculating number of WT juvenile individuals.
  
  N_at <- rpois(1, S_j * N_j0 + S_a * N_a0) #calculating number of adult individuals
  
  
  N_jtM <- rpois(1, N_a0M * R_aM) + New_jtM # calculating number of Mutant juveniles
  N_atM <- rpois(1, N_j0M * S_jM + S_aM * N_a0M) # calculating number of Mutant adults
  
  return(c(N_jt, N_at, N_jtM, N_atM))
}
print(simulate_one_gen(100, 100,0, 0, 2, 2, 0.1,0.1, 0.6, 0.6, 0.02))
```

## Simulate a population trajectory

```{r}
simulate_pop <- function(N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu, t_max) {
   # Create the vector in which to save the results
  pop_vector <- c(N_j0, N_a0, N_j0M, N_a0M) 
  # initiate the variables
  pop_new <- c(N_j0, N_a0, N_j0M, N_a0M)
  
  # run the simulation until generation t_max
  for (i in 1:t_max+1) {
    # redefine the current population one generation later
    pop_new <- simulate_one_gen(pop_new[1],pop_new[2],pop_new[3],pop_new[4], R_a,R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu)
    
    # add the new population sizes to the output vector
    pop_vector <- rbind(pop_vector,pop_new)
    # condition to stop the simulation before t_max: either the population exceeds 1.5 times the original population size, or it goes extinct
    if ( (pop_new[1]+pop_new[2]+ pop_new[3]+pop_new[4] >=10*(N_j0+ N_a0 + N_j0M+ N_a0M)) | (pop_new[1]+pop_new[2]+ pop_new[3]+pop_new[4]==0)) break }
  
  # add row and column names
  colnames(pop_vector) <- c("AC1", "AC2", "AC1M", "AC2M")
  rownames(pop_vector) <- (0:t_max)[1:length(pop_vector[,1])]
  
  return(pop_vector)
}
print(tail(simulate_pop(100, 100, 0,0, 2.5,2.5, 0.2,0.2, 0.6,0.6, 0.001, 1500)))


 
```

# basic plot with base r

```{r}
output <- simulate_pop(100, 100, 0,0, 1.8,2.5, 0.2,0.2, 0.6,0.6, 0.009, 1500)
print(tail(output))

x_range <- 0:(length(output[,1])-1)
# this plots the total population size
plot(x_range,output[,1]+output[,2],type='l',ylim=c(0,max(output[,1]+output[,2])),xlab = "Generation",ylab = "Population size")
# add number of Juvenile WT individuals
lines(x_range,output[,1], col="blue")
# add number of adult WT individuals
lines(x_range,output[,2], col="red")
#number of Juvenile Mutant individuals 
lines(x_range,output[,3], col = "green")
#number of adult mutant individuals
lines(x_range,output[,4], col = "yellow")

legend("right",
       c("WT Juvenile indidviduals", "WT Adult individuals", "Juvenile Mutant individuals", "Adult mutant individuals"),
       text.font = 3)
```

# pro version of plots by tobias with ggplot()

```{r}
install.packages("dplyr")
install.packages("tidyr")
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

```{r}


library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# having the simulation set as a variable
sim_data <- simulate_pop(100, 100, 0, 0, 2,2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.6, 0.8, 0.01, 1500)

#Convert matrix to Dataframe to help analysis
df <- as.data.frame(sim_data)

# these steps were generated using ai help: The rownames are the Generation numbers. Let's make them a proper column.
df$Generation <- as.numeric(rownames(df))

# Reshape from Wide to Long format for ggplot
# This creates a column "Age_Class" (AC1, AC2, etc.) and "Population_Size". 

#pivot_longer syntaxc first define what data you are looking at. here we are looking at df our data frame. cols defines which columns to convert into the long format. we want to convert our Age class collumns into long format. names_to defines what the new column name should be. 

df_long <- pivot_longer(
  df, 
  cols = c("AC1", "AC2", "AC1M", "AC2M"), 
  names_to = "Age_Class", 
  values_to = "Population_Size"
)


print(df_long)

ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Generation, y = Population_Size, color = Age_Class, linetype = Age_Class)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "AC1" = "lightgreen",
    "AC2" = "darkgreen",
    "AC1M" = "red",
    "AC2M" = "darkred")) +
  labs(title = "Simulating Evolutionary Rescue with 2 Age classes", subtitle = "Mutant Adults with higher survivability" , x = "Generations", y = "Population Size", color = "Age Classes", linetype = "Age Classes")+
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "AC1" = 1,
    "AC1M" = 1,
    "AC2" = 2,
    "AC2M" = 2))
  


```

## Compare juvenile- vs. adult survival rate increase in mutants

We have to figure out which ranges of survival rates make sense. So the growth rate of the wildtypes should be below 1 and for the mutants it should be more than 1 probably.

```{r}
#N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu, t_max
# set some parameters to fixed values
N_j0 <- 50
N_a0 <- 50
N_j0M <- 0
N_a0M <- 0
R_a <- 2
R_aM <- 2
mu <- 0.01
t_max <- 1000




# determine how often to run the simulation for each set of parameters
no_replicates <- 100

# initialize data table - where to collect the results
data_table <- c()

# Doing a parameter sweep
for (selection_on_jM in c(TRUE,FALSE)){
  for (s_coeff in seq(1, 2, 0.01)){
    S_j <- 0.2
    S_jM <- S_j * ifelse(selection_on_jM, s_coeff, 1)
    S_a <- 0.5
    S_aM <- S_a * ifelse(selection_on_jM, 1, s_coeff)
    
   
    i<-1
    repeat {
      # increase counter by one
      i<-i+1
      # run the simulation once
      one_run <- simulate_pop(N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu, t_max)
      # determine total population sizes
      total_size <- one_run[,1]+one_run[,2] +one_run[,3]+one_run[,4]
      # determine minimum population size
      min_size <- min(total_size)
      # determine (first) generation at which this population size occurred
      min_gen <- as.numeric(which(total_size==min_size)[1])
      # enter the data into the table
      data_table <- rbind(data_table,c(s_coeff,ifelse(selection_on_jM, "on_juv", "on_adults"),min_gen,min_size)) # note that we add the varying parameters (decay rate and selection coefficient) to the table too
      # stop the repeated computation after no_replicates times
      if(i>no_replicates) break
    }
  }  
}
 
# define column names of data table
colnames(data_table) <- c("s_coeff","ac_s","min_gen","no_min")
# show the first lines of the output





#define WT leslie matrix and get growth-rate

l_matrix_WT <- matrix(c(
  0, R_a,
  S_j, S_a
), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

all_eigen <- eigen(l_matrix_WT)
growth_rate_WT <- max(Re(all_eigen$values))
l_matrix_WT
growth_rate_WT

# define WT leslie matrix and get growth-rate
l_matrix_Mut <- matrix(c(
  0, R_aM,
  S_jM, S_aM
), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

all_eigen <- eigen(l_matrix_Mut)
growth_rate_Mut <- max(Re(all_eigen$values))
l_matrix_Mut
growth_rate_Mut

#making the matrix a table and making some values numeric to be able to calculate with them
df <- as.data.frame(data_table)
df$s_coeff <- as.numeric(df$s_coeff)
df$min_gen <- as.numeric(df$min_gen)
df$no_min <- as.numeric(df$no_min)

df$rescued <- df$no_min != 0

#try if the basic principle of gettint the resque-probability works
df_filter <- df[df$s_coeff == 1 & df$ac_s == "on_juv",]
print(mean(df_filter$rescued))

#creating a empty table to put the stuff to plot in
plot_table <- c()
for(x in unique(df$ac_s)){
 for(s in unique(df$s_coeff)){
  df_filter <- df[df$s_coeff == s & df$ac_s == x,]
  plot_table <- rbind(plot_table, c(mean(df_filter$rescued), x, s))
 } 
}

colnames(plot_table) <- c("resque prob.","ac_s","s_coeff")


```
